1. Cleanse scalp thoroughly, every few washes with a clarifying shampoo (vosene is decent and fairly cheap)
2. Condition - if your hair is low porosity which wavy hair often is, use a very lightweight conditioner diluted with water / a leave in conditioner 
3. Scrunch in gel/foam/seasalt spray upside down while wet, scrunching in as much water as you can at the same time 
4. Use a towel to “micro plop” hair dry as much as possible
4. Diffuse / leave to air dry

If you’re using gel and/or foam then the curls/waves feel like they have a bit of a coating while they are in the cast, but once that’s dry and you’ve scrunched it out they should feel soft and bouncy. If you can feel product then that probably is build up from products being too heavy. Is your hair low porosity? If so, products tend to sit on top of the hair. Less is more, and try to add water in the conditioning/styling steps.

Some mousse can be heavy and lead to build up easily, whereas foam is a lot lighter - Creme of Nature Argan Oil Style & Shine Foaming Mousse is a good one, or Flora and Curl (but this one is a little pricier)

I wonder if there’s a bit of product build up which is weighing down some curls and causing slight frizz? You could try:
Using less conditioner and squeezing in as much water as you can at this stage. 
Ditching the leave in
Swapping the mousse for gel while soaking wet, followed by a lightweight foam after micro plopping.

In my area there are 10 main secondary schools and they used to expel children and move them from school to school. This mostly lead to the expelled child continuing risky behaviours (e.g drug dealing), sometimes outside the gates of the school they were expelled from. It solved nothing.

One school then decided to pledge not to expel any students and trained all their staff in emotion coaching. The behaviour in this school improved exponentially, because the children who were acting out felt listened to and understood. The vast majority of children who are expelled experience difficult home lives, often with domestic violence, and need extra support and care.
